lines.text: Can a mini quiz beat another reread?
It can. It's called the testing effect.
Some reread them again and again. Others mostly tested themselves.
A week later, the rereaders remembered forty percent.
Rereading feels easier, so it feels like learning.
Close the book and quiz yourself. That's where memory gets built.

post.title: Stop Rereading. Do This Instead. #shorts
post.description: Quizzing yourself beats rereading. In Roediger & Karpicke (2006), students who repeatedly tested themselves recalled 61% of a passage a week later, versus 40% for students who kept rereading. That's the testing effect. #psychology #studytips #memory
